They aren't speaking Shelta at all. Shelta is influenced by English grammar, but it is also a mixture of Irish words, with the word order altered, syllables reversed, and many of the original words being Irish that have been altered or reversed. Carlos Fonseca explained that the original had been lost, so they decided to look for the one closest to the sequence - taken a second before or after the other - to replace it. "It was almost the same, only in this one I had a lost look," he said.

In American English, the word "billion" referred exclusively to a million millions (1,000,000,000,000). However, this is not common anymore, and the word has been used to mean one thousand million (1,000,000) since the early 20th century.

A recent study revealed that although NLP (natural-language processing) models are capable of incredible feats, their abilities are very much limited by the amount of context they receive. This limitation could cause difficulties for researchers who hope to use them to do things such as analyze ancient languages. In some cases, there are not enough written records or context available for NLP models to accurately process and understand the language.

The term "fatberg" is a compound of the words "fat" and "iceberg." The word was used in 2008 to describe "large, rock-like lumps of cooking fat" washing up on beaches in Wales, and by 2010 was used to refer to large masses of congealed fat and waste that clogged sewers.

In Sarah Waters' novel "The Paying Guests," the word "queer" is used to describe the unusual or remarkable, instead of its post-1922 meaning of homosexual. The novel's language bridges the divide between the past and the present, reflecting the changing meanings and connotations of words over time.
